_meta.indication: Prevention of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants at high risk for RDS; reduces the incidence of RDS at 24 hours and mortality due to RDS

pivotal_trials.trial_name: KL4-IRDS-06 (Study 1), the single pivotal efficacy study
pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal prophylaxis superiority trial (major efficacy study)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, multinational, randomized, double-blind, multi-dose, active-controlled superiority study comparing SURFAXIN to colfosceril palmitate (Exosurf), with beractant (Survanta) as an additional active comparator
pivotal_trials.population: Premature infants weighing 600 g to 1250 g at birth and 32 weeks or less gestational age, at high risk for RDS; participants from Europe and Latin America
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: incidence of RDS at 24 hours and RDS-related mortality through Day 14, with SURFAXIN vs. colfosceril palmitate (Exosurf) as the primary comparison for superiority
pivotal_trials.n: 1294 premature infants (SURFAXIN N=527, colfosceril palmitate N=509, beractant N=258)
pivotal_trials.result: SURFAXIN was superior to colfosceril palmitate on both co-primary endpoints: RDS at 24 hours 206 (39%) vs 240 (47%), P<0.01; RDS-related mortality through Day 14 25 (5%) vs 48 (9%), P<0.01. Reviewer analysis: 17% risk reduction in RDS at 24h (95% CI 5%, 28%; p=0.007) and 52% reduction in RDS-related mortality by 14 days (95% CI 24%, 69%; p=0.001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are administration-related: endotracheal tube reflux, pallor, endotracheal tube obstruction, and need for dose interruption, which occurred at higher incidence with SURFAXIN than comparator surfactants (e.g., Study 1 ETT reflux 18% vs 16%; pallor 9% vs 4%; dose interruption 9% vs 4%; ETT obstruction 6% vs 2%). Frequently occurring administration-related reactions include bradycardia, oxygen desaturation, reflux into the ETT, and airway/ETT obstruction.
target_moa: A synthetic lung surfactant that compensates for the deficiency of endogenous pulmonary surfactant in premature infants, lowering surface tension at the alveolar air-liquid interface and stabilizing alveoli against collapse; contains sinapultide (KL4 peptide) which mimics surfactant protein B (SP-B)
modality: Peptide-containing synthetic pulmonary surfactant (contains sinapultide, a 21-amino acid synthetic KL4 peptide)

rems.type: No post-marketing risk evaluation and mitigation strategies (REMS) are recommended

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Agency determined outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion

orphan_indication.text: SURFAXIN has an orphan drug designation for this indication (prevention of RDS in premature infants), an orphan disease

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
Surfaxin, like other surfactants for the prevention or treatment of RDS in premature infants has an orphan designation.

summary.text: SURFAXIN (lucinactant) was a 505(b)(2) NDA with orphan drug designation for prevention of RDS in premature infants. It was approved after multiple review cycles (originally submitted April 13, 2004; Approvable letter February 11, 2005; Complete Response action letter April 17, 2009; approval letter signed March 6, 2012), based on a single pivotal superiority study (KL4-IRDS-06) versus colfosceril palmitate. No advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received April 13, 2004, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Surfaxin (lucinactant) Intratracheal Suspension.

On February 11, 2005, the Division took an Approvable action on the application. The clinical recommendation was Approval, but there were substantial CMC deficiencies that resulted in the Approvable action.
The September 2, 2011, submission constituted a complete response to our April 17, 2009, action letter.

The demonstration of efficacy was provided by study KL4-IRDS-06, a multicenter, multinational, randomized study conducted outside the United States that compared Surfaxin® to Exosurf in a superiority design. A second active comparator, Survanta, was included for reference.
